wine.name: Grüner Veltliner Hund
wine.classification: Reserve, the fuller tier of the Weinviertel DAC
wine.sites: The Hundsleiten above Stetten, just north of Vienna, which gives the wine its name: flysch soils of clay and sandstone layers laced with quartz, a slope whose Grüner Veltliner has long stood out for its power and spice, as the house tells it.
wine.making: The grapes are selected in the vineyard and picked in the middle of October. After some eight hours on their skins they are pressed gently in a pneumatic press, and the wine is fermented and raised half in large wooden casks and half in stainless steel, as the house describes it.
wine.glass: Ripe pear, yellow apple and white pepper over a stony grip; powerful and full for a Grüner Veltliner, with lively acidity and a long, peppery finish.
wine.ageing: Ready a year after the harvest, it fills out over three to five years, and a ripe vintage holds for ten.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; no need to decant, though a young bottle opens with air; a white wine glass with a generous bowl.

label.means: The appellation's fuller tier: dry, at least thirteen per cent alcohol, with a hint of oak or botrytis allowed.
The vineyard name, short for the Hundsleiten above Stetten, where all its grapes grow.
Austria's own white grape, and the one grape the Weinviertel DAC admits.

records.table: Named for the Hundsleiten, a slope above Stetten just north of Vienna, Pfaffl's Grüner Veltliner Hund is a Weinviertel DAC Reserve. Powerful for the grape, it sets ripe pear and white pepper over a stony grip.
records.story: Before 1978 the Pfaffl farm at Stetten, just north of Vienna, lived mostly on grain, potatoes and livestock, with only a small plot of vines and a little wine. That year a young couple of the family took it over, and they set out to make wine the whole of the business. The family had long owned the Hundsleiten, a slope of flysch above the village whose Grüner Veltliner stood out for its power and spice, and the wine of that slope, labelled Hundsleiten in its earlier vintages and Hund since, became the house's calling card. From the 2002 vintage the Weinviertel was Austria's first DAC, an appellation for peppery Grüner Veltliner alone, and from the 2009 vintage it added a Reserve tier for riper, fuller wines; the Hund is labelled a Weinviertel DAC Reserve. The estate grew to vineyards across the southern Weinviertel and in Vienna, and the next generation of the family joined the founders in the cellar. Low yields, much hand work and a late harvest, as the house puts it, give the Hund its weight. It teaches the Reserve style: Grüner Veltliner with the pepper of the classic tier and the body to stand beside a main course.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Hommage
others.note: A Weinviertel DAC Reserve from very old vines on the Kirchenberg of Grossebersdorf, fermented with wild yeasts in acacia casks.

traps: Another Weinviertel winery bears the Pfaffl name: the house of the Hund is R&A Pfaffl of Stetten, so read the initials on the label.
Hund means dog in German, but on this label it is the vineyard: the Hundsleiten above Stetten, printed in full on earlier vintages.

questions.exp: Reserve is the Weinviertel DAC's fuller tier: dry, at least thirteen per cent alcohol, with a hint of oak or botrytis allowed; it asks for no long ageing, and the DAC admits Grüner Veltliner alone.

questions.exp: They took over the mixed farm in 1978; 2002 is the first vintage of the Weinviertel DAC, Austria's first, more than twenty years later.

wine.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Bürsting
wine.sites: The Bürsting, a high plateau at the end of a cellar lane in Poysdorf, on deep, moist loam, with vines planted in the early 1960s; the gravel of the Sauberg meets its loam on the neighbouring slope.
wine.making: Picked by hand into small crates in October, the grapes rest about a day on their skins before pressing. The must is fermented with wild yeasts, partly in used 500 litre barrels and partly in small steel tanks, the share of each varying with the vintage.
wine.glass: Yellow pear, quince and white pepper over a dense, creamy texture; broad and savoury, with ripe acidity and a long, peppery close.
wine.ageing: Approachable within two years of the harvest, it gains depth over five to eight, and a strong vintage lasts a decade or more.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for half an hour to let it open; a white wine glass with a generous bowl.

label.means: The single vineyard; Austrian law asks for the word Ried before a vineyard's name.
Organic: the house's own sheets describe the Bürsting as organically grown.

records.table: Vines of the early 1960s on a loam plateau at the end of a Poysdorf cellar lane give Ebner-Ebenauer's Grüner Veltliner Ried Bürsting. Wild yeasts, and used barrels for part of it, leave it dense and peppery, a white for roast pork.
records.story: The family behind the house has grown wine around Poysdorf, in the north east of the Weinviertel, for many generations, fourteen by its own count, and its cellar, cut six metres into the ground on three levels, is held to be some four hundred years old. The farm above it burnt almost to the ground in 1945, at the end of the Second World War, and was rebuilt; grandparents with ties to France and Italy brought something of the Mediterranean into the new house, as the family tells it. In the early years of this century a young couple married, took over the husband's family estate and gave it their joined names, Ebner-Ebenauer, and they set about vinifying each parcel on its own. They farmed organically and let the must run into the cellar by gravity, without pumps. In 2022 Falstaff named the couple its Winemakers of the Year. In 2024 the house was among the thirteen founders of the Weinviertel association of the ÖTW, the traditional estates that classify Austria's Erste Lagen, and its Sauberg and Hermannschachern carry that rank. The Bürsting, vines of the early 1960s on the deep loam beside the Sauberg, shows the warmth and weight Grüner Veltliner can find at Poysdorf.

wine.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Äussere Bergen
wine.classification: Reserve of the Weinviertel DAC; an Erste Lage of the ÖTW, printed 1ÖTW
wine.sites: The Äussere Bergen, the south easternmost vineyard of Schrattenthal, at about 280 metres: weathered granite of the Manhartsberg under a cover of loess.
wine.making: Picked by hand early in October, the grapes rest some eighteen hours on their skins before pressing. The wine is raised in large wooden casks, in some vintages with a share in steel, and the house gives it about fifteen months before bottling.
wine.glass: Ripe apricot, baked apple and white pepper over a salty, stony grip; velvety and full, with fresh acidity and a long finish touched with tobacco.
wine.ageing: Broad and open two years after the harvest, it drinks well for eight to ten years from a ripe vintage.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius, after half an hour in a decanter when young; a white wine glass with a generous bowl.

label.means: The appellation's fuller tier: dry, at least thirteen per cent alcohol, with a hint of oak allowed.
An Erste Lage, a site classified by the ÖTW, the association of Austria's traditional wine estates.
The vineyard's name, the outer hills, the south easternmost slope of Schrattenthal.

records.table: Out in the cool west of the Weinviertel, at Schrattenthal near Retz, Zull grows its Grüner Veltliner Ried Äussere Bergen on granite under loess: a DAC Reserve raised in large casks, ripe and velvety with white pepper, that suits roast veal.
records.story: Schrattenthal, a small town on the edge of the Waldviertel, appears in a document of 1220, as the house recounts, and the house at number nine is where the Zull story begins: a great grandfather of the family married into it, at a time when wine was one crop among many on a mixed farm. In the 1980s a later generation gave up the rest and turned the farm wholly to wine, by the family's telling. Its vineyards lie on weathered granite of the Manhartsberg under a thin coat of loess, and cold winds from the higher Waldviertel to the west cool the grapes as they ripen. The Äussere Bergen is the house's Reserve from one slope: the Weinviertel, Austria's first DAC from the 2002 vintage, for Grüner Veltliner alone, added that fuller tier from the 2009 vintage. When thirteen estates founded the ÖTW's Weinviertel association in 2024, Zull was one of them, and the association ranks the Äussere Bergen an Erste Lage. The western Weinviertel comes through in it: granite, cool nights and Grüner Veltliner of ripe fruit and firm line.

others.name: Riesling Schrattenthal vom Urgestein
others.note: The house's village Riesling, from the primary rock around Schrattenthal.

traps: Zull's granite lies in the far west by the Manhartsberg; most of the Weinviertel grows on loess, sand and gravel, so this is not the region's usual soil.
The Äussere Bergen is a single vineyard of Schrattenthal, not a village of its own, and the wine carries the Reserve tier.

wine.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Laa 8000
wine.classification: Reserve of the Weinviertel DAC; an Erste Lage of the ÖTW, printed 1ÖTW
wine.sites: The Ried Laa at Hohenwarth, on the western edge of the Weinviertel: a very chalky soil with white lines of lime plain on the surface, planted at about eight thousand vines to every ten thousand square metres.
wine.making: Fermented with wild yeasts in stainless steel and raised in steel for some ten months, so that site and grape alone shape it. The close planting forces the roots deep against drought and keeps each vine's crop small, which the house holds is the source of the wine's concentration.
wine.glass: Lime, green pear and white pepper over a chalky, salty core; taut and juicy, with lively acidity, close concentration and a long, peppery finish.
wine.ageing: Tight in its first two years, it opens over three to six and lasts ten or more from a strong vintage.
wine.serve: At 10 to 12 degrees Celsius in a broad bowled white wine glass; give a young bottle half an hour in a decanter.

label.means: The planting density: about eight thousand vines to every ten thousand square metres in the Ried Laa.
An Erste Lage, a site classified by the ÖTW, the association of Austria's traditional wine estates.
The appellation's fuller tier: dry and at least thirteen per cent alcohol.

records.table: Eight thousand vines to every ten thousand square metres: that is the figure on Setzer's Grüner Veltliner Ried Laa 8000, from a chalky Erste Lage at Hohenwarth. Wild yeasts and steel keep it taut, salty and peppery, a wine for trout or veal.
records.story: Wine has been made at Hohenwarth, on the western edge of the Weinviertel, since at least 1360, the house recounts, and the Setzer family has worked here since 1705, by its own account. For most of those centuries the estate was a mixed farm, with vines beside crops and livestock. Only in 2001 did the family lease out its farmland and become a wine estate alone. A year later, with the 2002 vintage, the Weinviertel became Austria's first DAC, for Grüner Veltliner alone, and its Reserve tier for fuller wines came with the 2009 vintage. On their chalkiest site, the Ried Laa, the family planted Grüner Veltliner at about eight thousand vines to every ten thousand square metres, close enough to force the roots deep, and they named the wine for the figure. Setzer was one of the thirteen founding estates of the ÖTW's Weinviertel association in 2024, and the house prints the Laa as an Erste Lage. The house names the 8000 one of its two flagships, beside a Roter Veltliner from the Ried Kreimelberg, and it argues for dense planting in a dry land.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Große Reserve Ried Laa
others.note: From the same site, in the fullest tier of the Weinviertel DAC, held longer in the cellar than a Reserve.

others.name: Roter Veltliner Ried Kreimelberg

The 8000 is a Reserve, not the Große Reserve: Setzer makes a Große Reserve from the same Ried Laa, held longer before release.

wine.name: Grüner Veltliner Röschitz
wine.classification: The classic tier of the Weinviertel DAC, beneath Reserve and Große Reserve
wine.sites: Parcels in and around Röschitz on the eastern slopes of the Manhartsberg, on loess and weathered primary rock with granite among it.
wine.making: The grapes come only from the house's vineyards at Röschitz. The must is fermented in stainless steel and the wine kept in steel for an early bottling; the rules of the classic tier allow no taste of oak or botrytis.
wine.glass: Green apple, yellow grapefruit peel and white pepper; light and lively, with crisp acidity, a faint bitter twist of lemon pith and a clean, dry finish.
wine.ageing: Made to be drunk young, within one to three years of the harvest, while its pepper and freshness last.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; no need to decant; a white wine glass.

label.means: Austria's first DAC, for Grüner Veltliner alone: dry, peppery and with no taste of oak.
The village of the house and its vineyards, printed after the grape's name on the label.
Organic: the family farms its vineyards organically, and the wine is certified so.

records.table: Gruber Röschitz's Grüner Veltliner Röschitz is the Weinviertel DAC in its classic tier from loess and granite around Röschitz on the Manhartsberg. Fermented in steel and bottled young, it is light, dry and full of white pepper, a glass for the Heuriger table.
records.story: For more than two hundred years, as the family tells the story, the Grubers have grown wine at Röschitz, on the eastern slopes of the Manhartsberg in the north west of the Weinviertel. As late as 1970 the grandfather of the present generation ran a mixed farm of crops, livestock and vines, and the estate was built up from it around Grüner Veltliner. When the Weinviertel became Austria's first DAC with the 2002 vintage, it was made for peppery Grüner Veltliner alone; a bottle with no Reserve on its label is the classic tier, dry, fresh and free of any taste of oak or botrytis. In 2012 three siblings took over their parents' estate, sharing the vineyards, the cellar and the selling between them, and they farm it organically. Röschitz is not typical Weinviertel ground: where most of the region grows on gravel, sand and loess, the soils here are poor primary rock with granite under shallow loess. The house's name stands among the thirteen that founded the ÖTW's Weinviertel association in 2024. Pour its Röschitz to show the classic tier: the plain, peppery Grüner Veltliner the appellation was made for.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Reipersberg
others.note: A Weinviertel DAC from the highest part of Röschitz, where granite predominates, by the house's account.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Mühlberg
others.note: A Weinviertel DAC Reserve from a single Ried of Röschitz.

traps: A Weinviertel DAC with no Reserve on the label is the classic tier: at most six grams of sugar to the litre, with no taste of oak or botrytis.
Gruber Röschitz is one family estate of the village of Röschitz; the place name is part of the house's name, not a second producer.

cards.front: Gruber Röschitz: on what soils do the vines around Röschitz grow?
cards.back: Poor primary rock with granite, under shallow loess, on the eastern slopes of the Manhartsberg.

cards.front: Gruber Röschitz: since when has the house been a member of the ÖTW, by its own account?
cards.back: Since May 2024, among the founders of the ÖTW's Weinviertel association.

questions.q: A guest asks whether Gruber Röschitz's Grüner Veltliner Weinviertel DAC has seen oak. What is true?
opts: No: the classic tier allows no taste of oak
Yes: it spends a year in new barriques
Yes: it is raised in old acacia casks
No: it is a sparkling wine made in tank
questions.exp: The classic Weinviertel DAC must show no oak or botrytis, and the house ferments it in stainless steel; a hint of oak is allowed only in a Reserve.

questions.q: In which year did three Gruber siblings take over their parents' estate at Röschitz?
questions.exp: The siblings took over in 2012; 2002 is the first vintage of the Weinviertel DAC, 2024 the year the house helped found the ÖTW's Weinviertel association.

report: Thin region rule: the house is a family estate known for a well made, widely poured DAC wine rather than a single famous bottling, and the record says so; the pick stands, no swap to Weinrieder proposed.

The label form has moved: older vintages print Weinviertel DAC Klassik Grüner Veltliner, recent ones Weinviertel DAC Grüner Veltliner Röschitz with no Klassik; the lint holds the name to the plan's words, and the checker may wish a swap of the wine's name to Grüner Veltliner Röschitz.
Founded is empty: one regional chamber article gives 1814 for the family's farming at Röschitz, a retailer only more than two hundred years; the story says the latter, as the family tells it.

The steel fermentation, the temperature, the lees and the 280 to 340 metres come from the house's sheet for its DAC wine; that the wine was also bottled young rests on its one to three year window on the house's own pages.
The family's work for Stift Altenburg and Schloss Maissau is the house's claim alone and is left out.

changed: story and questions: organic farming from 2013 was unconfirmed (neither the house's pages nor the chamber's report give a year) and is cut from the story, the label and the story question; the question now asks the year of the takeover, 2012, which the chamber's report and the company register confirm.

story: three of six siblings now three siblings; wine made largely for the household now the grandfather's mixed farm of 1970, the chamber's words; Grüner Veltliner as about half the vineyards cut as volatile; the ÖTW founding dated 2024.
story: was the Weinviertel DAC of 2003; now from the 2002 vintage, as Austrian Wine gives it.

wine.sites and wine.making: the 280 to 340 metres, the pneumatic press, the twenty degrees and the weeks on the lees were not confirmed and are cut; steel fermentation stands on an importer's listing and the Röschitz fruit on another.
others: the Reipersberg's terraces and sixty year old vines and the Mühlberg's mill were unconfirmed; now the house's own granite for the Reipersberg and a plain Reserve listing for the Mühlberg.
cards: the second card now asks for the ÖTW membership of May 2024, the house's own date, since the question asks for 2012.
sources: the house's family page and Falstaff blog post replaced by the chamber's report and an importer's listing.

Swap applied by the read-together agent on 2026-11-16: the pick's wine is now Grüner Veltliner Röschitz in plan.json, with the swap in the group's swaps, and wine.name (was Grüner Veltliner Weinviertel DAC) now Grüner Veltliner Röschitz; house and key kept.
open: Some export listings still print Klassik for the same wine.
The family's more than two hundred years: the chamber gives wine growing since 1814; founded stays empty.
